paras: The Texarkana pest house whitecap raid was an attack in early April 1903 by a band of "whitecappers" on the Texarkana pest house, whose only occupant was a lone Black man. Armed citizens met the raiders with a volley and they dispersed; no one was reported hurt. The episode drew notice chiefly because townspeople organized to defend the occupant, which the San Antonio Daily Light praised in an editorial.
The papers describe the building at Texarkana as the "negro pest house." According to the San Antonio Daily Light, its only occupant at the time was a single Black man, whom it did not name.

A band described as whitecappers raided the pest house. Citizens of Texarkana, who had organized to defend the man inside, fired a volley at the raiders, who "quickly disperse[d]." The report gives no number of raiders, no names, no motive and no casualties on either side.
No report of arrests, an investigation or charges against the raiders appears in the coverage, and the fate of the man in the pest house is not reported.

The raid reached the press as a single line among the San Antonio Daily Light's "Telegraph Brevities" of April 6, between a church-floor collapse at Atlanta and royal gossip from Berlin. The next day the same paper returned to it in a short editorial paragraph, saying that Texarkana "did herself proud" in defending "that lone negro" against "the inhumanity of the whitecappers." The editorial aimed its condemnation at the whitecappers and its praise at the townspeople, while the man defended remained nameless in both items.
No other white paper and no Black newspaper reporting the raid was found, so the episode is known only from these two San Antonio items.
